Subject: Audit export cadence / timeline question

Hi Logan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're moving toward final internal approval but two items came up from our security and compliance team that are gating sign-off:

1) A scheduled audit export (CSV) delivered daily to our S3 bucket with a guaranteed ordering and schema (they want the same columns as the sample we saw).
2) A retention metadata field added to the export so our downstream pipeline can automatically enforce data retention policies.

Can Redwood commit to delivering a first-pass implementation of the scheduled export and retention field before our board sign-off on May 20? Summit is prepared to sign the SOW immediately if we have a written commitment with a short rollout plan and acceptance criteria.

Attaching the SOW draft and a sample of the audit rows we expect.

--

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 03 May 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Audit export cadence / timeline question — priority ask from Summit

Thanks for flagging, Logan. High level: the feature splits into two workstreams — (A) an export pipeline that can materialize daily CSVs to an external S3 with stable schema and ordering guarantees; (B) adding a small metadata field to the export payload and wiring it through our retention/metadata contract.

Considerations:
- For hosted customers, daily export job is straightforward but needs an opt-in per-account S3 connector + secure credentials handling and job scheduling.
- Ordering guarantees mean we need deterministic sort keys (we already have event-timestamp + sequence but will need a formalized contract).
- Retention metadata is low development cost but touches our audit schema and requires docs and a simple migration strategy for older exports.

Estimate (ballpark):
- Core export plumbing + S3 connector: 3-4 weeks (one eng + infra support).
- Ordering contract and schema doc + QA: 1 week.
- Retention-field wiring + docs: 2-3 days.
- End-to-end testing & sign-off: 3 days.

Total: ~5 weeks if we can start next week. That's tight for a May 20 commitment given approvals and QA. Alternatives to accelerate:
1) Nightly manual export where Support runs the job and pushes to the customer's bucket (2 business days turnaround) — lowest dev work, operational overhead.
2) Beta automation with limited guarantees but earlier delivery (approx 2 weeks) — provide a clear risk statement and acceptance criteria.

I'll need an eng owner and infra approval before committing. Ben / Karthik — can you confirm capacity and whether infra has any blocking items?

-Marissa
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 May 2027 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Audit export cadence / timeline question — priority ask from Summit

Agree with Marissa's breakdown. A few engineering notes from infra side:
- The S3 connector work is mostly reusing existing transfer agents, but we'll need a secure credential flow (we should use short-lived STS creds or presigned put links). That adds ~3-4 days of infra and security review.
- If Summit requires schema immutability (can't change column order/fields) we should version the export contract; adding versioning support adds ~1 week.

Realistically, with current sprint allocations we could aim for a beta automation in 2 weeks if we deprioritize other planned work. Full production-grade delivery with versioning and formal ordering guarantees is ~5 weeks.

Proposal to close deal quickly:
- Offer a written commitment to deliver a documented nightly CSV export (beta) in 10 business days with explicit acceptance criteria. Scope: daily scheduled job, same-column order as sample, retention metadata included as a named column, delivered via presigned upload to Summit's S3.
- Follow-on: production hardening + versioned contract within 5 weeks of the beta launch.

If Sales is comfortable with a two-step commitment, we can provide dates and language for the SOW. Need Logan to confirm commercial terms (SOW milestone and acceptance), and Priyom to confirm legal safety for presigned uploads.

-ben
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime

Subject: Re: Audit export cadence / timeline question — proposed plan and dates

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks for the note and the patience while we scoped this internally. Proposed commercial/technical plan to unblock Summit's approval: 

1) Beta nightly CSV export (presigned upload to Summit S3) — target delivery: 2027-05-16. Scope: daily scheduled job, CSV schema matches the attached sample, includes new column `retention_policy_days`. This will be delivered as a beta feature; Redwood will provide a runbook and test sample for Summit to validate.

2) Production hardening & contract versioning — target delivery: 2027-06-20. Scope: documented ordering guarantees, versioned schema support, and automated scheduled exports with SLA monitoring.

We will add the beta milestone and acceptance criteria to the SOW and request Summit sign-off on the two-phase schedule. Legal/Delivery notes: we plan to use presigned PUT uploads for the beta (short-lived tokens) — Priyom, please advise if this needs to be called out in the SOW or requires additional clauses.

If Summit agrees, we'll issue an SOW amendment for these milestones and dates (HubSpot ref HS-78921 / Deal SUM-2027-0421).

Please confirm and I will send the amended SOW + DocuSign link.

Best —
